mechanism_narrative: The steady four-week improvement in RETAIL_REC from -32.9 to -26.7, together with rising TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, signals a reopening trajectory that will lift retail and recreation mobility further over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each week from -32.9 to -26.7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days despite continued improvement in RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT crosses above -31.0 percent change from baseline, it signals sufficient return of commuting to sustain retail footfall, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -31.0 percent change from baseline.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays above -31.0 for at least two weeks but RETAIL_REC declines or is flat over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Joint weekly gains in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reinforce each other, indicating a broad return to routine mobility that spills over into retail and recreation, pushing RETAIL_REC up over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise at least 1.0 point week-on-week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -21.1 to -18.7 and TRANSIT from -33.9 to -30.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise at least 1.0 point week-on-week but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than over the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility above 10 percent change from baseline indicates work-from-home behavior that curbs discretionary retail trips, so RETAIL_REC will fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 10.0 percent change from baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above 10.0 in all four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 10.0 for four weeks but RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Policy easing is revealed by improving TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC; as restrictions loosen further, retail and recreation mobility will continue to recover over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.9 to -30.6 and RETAIL_REC from -32.9 to -26.7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days even though TRANSIT continues to improve or stays stable.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GROCERY_PHARM alongside elevated RESIDENTIAL shows continued caution and essential-only shopping, diverting spending from retail and recreation, so RETAIL_REC will decline over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is positive at 3.7 and RESIDENTIAL is 10.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM > 2.0 and RESIDENTIAL > 10.0 but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than over the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Winter in Sydney suppresses parks but not retail; the recent PARKS rebound from -23.3 to -13.4 signals outdoor activity that correlates with retail footfall, predicting higher RETAIL_REC over one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -23.3 to -13.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS improves or stays above -15.0 but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than over the previous 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT is the strongest leading indicator; two consecutive weekly gains in TRANSIT signal a durable return to commuting that lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 1.0 point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -33.9 to -30.6 over four weeks with steady weekly gains
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves by more than 1.0 point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than over the previous 14 days.
